title: The Crown Beneath the Castle
description: Explore an abandoned castle, uncover its secrets, and recover the missing royal crown.

text: Welcome to the Forgotten Gardens, {player.name}.
You stand before an enormous stone fountain. Its basin is dry, and weeds have grown between the surrounding stones.
Beyond the garden stands an ancient castle. Its gates are open, but the grounds appear to have been abandoned for many years.
A weathered plaque reads: 'The crown belongs to those who can unlock the past.'
There are paths leading in several directions. Perhaps someone left something behind.
You follow a narrow path north of the fountain.
Tall hedges surround you, forming a maze of green corridors.
A stone statue stands nearby. It depicts a woman holding a small bird.
The inscription beneath it reads: 'A kingdom may lose its riches, but never its memories.'
You discover a small garden plaza.
At its center stands a statue of the castle's former queen.
Her outstretched hand points toward the eastern gardens.
A faded inscription reads: 'The gardener kept what the guards overlooked.'
You wonder whether the old gardener left anything useful behind.
The hedges become increasingly dense as you travel east.
You find an old wooden bench covered in moss.
Someone has carved a message into its surface: 'When the fountain runs dry, follow the roses below.'
The carving appears to be quite old.
You reach a secluded corner of the gardens.
An ornamental basin sits beneath a large tree. Although the water has disappeared, something glimmers at the bottom.
It looks like a silver coin bearing the castle's royal emblem.
Perhaps it once belonged to a visitor or a member of the royal family.
A narrow staircase leads down toward an old stone platform.
You recognize the platform as part of the fountain's original water system.
A series of pipes runs underground, but most have collapsed.
There is a small inscription on the nearest pipe: 'Water flows where the old gardener wills it.'
You walk along a cobblestone path beside the fountain.
The path is lined with empty flowerbeds and broken lanterns.
One lantern still contains a little oil, although its flame has long since gone out.
You can see the castle walls rising in the distance.
You discover the remains of an ornamental pool.
A decorative stone bridge crosses its center.
The bridge appears sturdy enough to support your weight.
Beyond it, a narrow path leads toward the eastern garden.
You follow the path south of the fountain.
The roses growing here have become tangled and overgrown.
Despite the neglected garden, several flowers are still blooming.
An old wooden sign reads: 'Gardener's quarters ahead.'
You discover a small gardener's shed hidden behind the rose bushes.
Inside, you find a workbench, a broken watering can, and several empty pots.
A rusty iron key rests beneath an old gardening journal.
The journal contains only one readable sentence: 'The eastern garden gate protects the castle courtyard.'
You follow a narrow trail east of the gardener's shed.
An old wooden cart has been abandoned beside the path.
Its wheels are broken, and its contents have long since rotted away.
You notice several footprints in the dirt, although they appear to be many years old.
You reach an old water pump.
The handle is stiff, and the machinery beneath it is completely rusted.
A small plaque reads: 'The gardener's key opens the eastern gate.'
Beyond the pump, a narrow path leads toward what appears to be a fortified entrance.
You find a narrow path leading toward an iron gate.
The gate is decorated with the same royal emblem found on the fountain.
A keyhole is visible in its center.
You stand before the eastern garden gate.
Beyond it lies the castle courtyard.
The gate is locked, and the ironwork has begun to rust.

success.message: The iron key turns with a loud click. The gate slowly swings open, revealing the castle courtyard.

failure.message: The gate refuses to move. You need the old gardener's iron key.

text: You enter the castle courtyard.
The enormous courtyard is surrounded by tall stone walls and elaborate archways.
A dry fountain occupies its center. Its statue depicts a knight holding a shield.
Several passages lead deeper into the castle.
To the west is the royal library. To the east is an old chapel.
A massive door stands to the north, while a covered passage leads south.

success.message: The moon and sun keys fit into the two locks. The enormous doors open, revealing the entrance to the royal vault.

failure.message: The northern doors remain sealed. Two keyholes are visible: one shaped like a crescent moon and the other like a sun. You need both keys.

text: You enter a covered arcade beneath the courtyard.
The ceiling is decorated with paintings of former kings and queens.
Most of the paintings have been damaged by water, but one remains remarkably intact.
It depicts a king holding a golden crown, surrounded by two knights.
The covered arcade opens into a quiet passage.
An old marble fountain stands against the wall.
A message has been carved into its base: 'The moon watches over knowledge. The sun guards the sacred.'
You suspect this passage may offer a way back to the gardens.

success.message: You pass through an old service passage and return to the Forgotten Gardens.

text: You discover a narrow alcove beneath the arcade.
Several old maintenance tools are scattered across the floor.
A faded drawing depicts the courtyard's original layout.
One section of the drawing has been marked with a small circle.
You reach the far end of the lower courtyard.
A large stone sundial stands against the wall.
Its shadow appears to point toward the northern doors.
A small inscription reads: 'Only when the sun and moon unite shall the crown be revealed.'
You discover an unusual stone doorway hidden behind a decorative pillar.
A circular indentation is carved into the center of the door.
It appears that something once served as a key.

success.message: The silver coin fits perfectly into the indentation. A hidden mechanism activates, and the stone doorway slides open.

failure.message: The circular indentation appears to require a coin bearing the royal emblem.

text: You enter the royal library.
Thousands of books line the walls, many of them covered in dust.
A large wooden desk stands in the center of the room.
The library appears to have been abandoned in a hurry.
Somewhere among these books may be information about the royal vault.
You enter the main reading hall.
Rows of wooden tables stretch across the room.
Several books remain open, as though their readers simply stood up and left.
One book describes the history of the castle's royal family.
It mentions that two keys were created to protect the royal vault.
You find a small reading room overlooking the gardens.
A large window lets in a beam of sunlight.
A book rests on the windowsill. Its title reads: 'The History of the Royal Crown.'
According to the book, the crown was hidden away after the disappearance of the last king.
You enter a room filled with maps.
Some depict the castle grounds, while others show distant kingdoms.
One map shows a hidden passage connecting the courtyard to the royal vault.
Someone has written a note beneath the map: 'The two keys were entrusted to separate guardians.'
You enter the restricted archive.
A heavy wooden table is covered in old documents.
Most of the papers are too damaged to read, but one describes the moon key.
It states that the key was kept by the royal archivist, who refused to leave the library.
You discover the royal archivist's desk.
An old chair sits behind it, facing the library entrance.
A small drawer contains several letters and a dusty journal.
Beneath the journal lies an ornate silver key decorated with a crescent moon.
This must be the moon key described in the archive.
You discover a balcony overlooking the main reading hall.
The railing is decorated with carvings of stars and constellations.
An inscription reads: 'Knowledge outlives the kingdom that created it.'
You can see the courtyard from here.
You find a small genealogy alcove.
Portraits of former royal family members hang along the walls.
A portrait of the last king has been damaged, but his name remains visible.
A plaque beneath the portrait reads: 'King Aldric, keeper of the crown.'
This room contains records of the castle's oldest inhabitants.
A shelf has collapsed, leaving books scattered across the floor.
One surviving document describes the royal archivist's final days.
The archivist apparently believed the moon key should never leave the library.
You enter a narrow section of the library known as the Dust Stacks.
The shelves are packed tightly together.
You find several books about ancient mechanical devices.
A diagram shows a complicated locking mechanism similar to the one protecting the royal vault.
A fallen bookshelf has created a small opening behind the stacks.
Inside, you discover a hidden compartment.
A torn page has been carefully folded and placed inside.
It appears to be part of an old royal document. Perhaps it was hidden for safekeeping.
You enter the royal chapel.
Tall stained-glass windows cast colorful patterns across the floor.
Rows of wooden pews face an elaborate altar.
The chapel is quiet, and the air smells faintly of old incense.
A plaque near the entrance reads: 'The sun brings light to those who seek it.'
You walk between the rows of wooden pews.
Several hymn books remain on their seats.
One contains a handwritten note: 'The keeper of the sun key served beneath the chapel's eastern window.'
You enter a small room beside the chapel.
A wooden cabinet contains old ceremonial clothing.
A golden symbol of the sun hangs above the cabinet.
The symbol appears to be connected to the chapel's history.
You discover a narrow staircase leading upward.
The walls are decorated with paintings of the sun rising over distant mountains.
The paintings become progressively brighter as you climb.
At the top, a small passage leads toward the eastern altar.
You reach the eastern altar.
A large stained-glass window depicts a golden sun surrounded by rays of light.
Beneath the window rests an ornate golden key.
Its handle is shaped like a sun.
You recognize it as the sun key described in the library records.
You find a small choir loft.
An old wooden music stand holds a collection of handwritten songs.
One song is dedicated to the last royal family.
Its final verse reads: 'When moon and sun are brought together, the sleeping crown shall awaken.'
You enter the chapel's bell chamber.
A large bell hangs above the room, suspended from an ancient wooden frame.
Its rope has been cut, and the bell is silent.
A small inscription reads: 'The bell was last rung on the night the crown disappeared.'
You discover an old storage room beside the bell chamber.
Broken candles and wooden boxes are scattered across the floor.
Among the debris, you find a heavy bronze bell clapper.
It is no longer attached to the chapel bell, but it appears to have been carefully preserved.
You enter a narrow passage beside the chapel.
A row of small stained-glass windows depicts scenes from the castle's history.
One image shows two keys being presented before a large golden door.
The illustration confirms what you learned in the library.
You return to the chapel's central aisle.
The afternoon light streams through the windows.
For a moment, the royal sun emblem on the altar appears to glow.
The chapel must have been an important place to the former royal family.
The stone doorway closes behind you.
You have entered the royal crypt, an underground chamber beneath the castle.
The air is cold, and the walls are covered with the names of former members of the royal family.
A narrow staircase leads deeper underground.
You descend into the main crypt corridor.
Stone sarcophagi line both walls.
Each bears the name of a former ruler.
A small plaque reads: 'Here rest those who protected the crown.'
You reach a large underground chamber.
The ceiling is supported by thick stone pillars.
An elaborate mural depicts the founding of the castle.
At the center of the mural, a knight kneels before a king holding a golden crown.
You discover a small tomb decorated with silver ornaments.
A stone inscription identifies its occupant as Sir Rowan, a knight who served the royal family.
A small ceremonial relic has been placed beside the sarcophagus.
It appears to have survived the passage of time remarkably well.
You enter a narrow chamber filled with old weapons and shields.
Most are badly corroded.
One shield still bears the castle's royal emblem.
An inscription reads: 'A true guardian protects what cannot be replaced.'
You discover a small memorial room.
Candles have been placed before several stone tablets.
Each tablet honors a person who protected the castle during difficult times.
The final tablet bears the name of the last royal archivist.
You enter an underground archive.
Old scrolls and stone tablets are stored in wooden cabinets.
One scroll tells the story of the castle's final days.
It claims the king ordered the crown hidden away to prevent it from falling into the wrong hands.
A small chamber lies beyond the archive.
The walls are covered in faded writing.
Most of it is impossible to read, but one sentence remains clear:
'The greatest treasure is not gold, but the memories preserved within these walls.'
You reach the far end of the crypt.
A stone bench stands beneath an ancient mural.
The mural depicts the castle before it was abandoned.
For a moment, you imagine what these halls must have looked like when the kingdom was alive.
The massive doors close behind you.
You have entered the royal vault.
Gold decorations cover the walls, although much of the treasure appears to have been removed.
A long passage leads deeper into the chamber.
The air is remarkably clean, as though someone maintained this place long after the rest of the castle was abandoned.
You enter the Hall of Guardians.
Large stone statues stand on either side of the passage.
Each statue holds a different weapon.
An inscription reads: 'Those who enter seeking riches shall leave empty-handed.'
You reach a gallery filled with royal portraits.
The paintings depict generations of kings and queens.
At the end of the gallery hangs a portrait of King Aldric.
He is holding the golden crown that disappeared many years ago.
You enter a small chamber containing several empty treasure chests.
Their contents have long since been removed.
A handwritten note rests inside one of the chests:
'The crown was never meant to be a symbol of wealth. It was a symbol of responsibility.'
You enter the innermost chamber of the royal vault.
A golden crown rests upon a stone pedestal.
It is decorated with precious stones and the royal emblem.
After all these years, the missing crown has finally been found.
You carefully take the crown. The castle's greatest secret has been uncovered!
Congratulations, {player.name}! You have completed The Crown Beneath the Castle.
You discover a small side chamber.
A collection of royal documents is stored in a locked display case.
One document describes the final days of King Aldric's reign.
It appears that the king deliberately hid the crown to protect the kingdom's history.
You enter the Chamber of Mirrors.
Several tall mirrors line the walls.
Although their surfaces are dusty, they still reflect the room clearly.
The final mirror is decorated with the same crescent moon and sun symbols found on the vault doors.
You realize that the two keys were always intended to be used together.
